note: Traces the line from reasoning prompts to autonomous agents, which is the capability jump that changes an audit risk assessment.
title: Igniting Language Intelligence: The Hitchhiker's Guide from Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Language Agents
explain_beginner: This survey explains how large language models can reason through complex tasks by using chain of thought prompting. Instead of jumping straight to an answer, the model writes out its reasoning before giving a result. That approach can improve results and make the model easier to understand, control, and adapt. The paper then follows how this reasoning method has been extended into self directed language agents, which can follow instructions and act in different settings. It reviews the basics of chain of thought, how the idea has changed, and how agents are being built with it. It also lists future questions about generalization, efficiency, customization, scaling, and safety.
explain_business: For executives, this survey matters because it maps a shift from models that only answer questions to agents that can take direction and act in settings. That shift can change how work is automated and how risk is assessed. The paper reviews chain of thought reasoning, which asks a model to show its reasoning steps, and explains how that approach supports more capable agents. It also flags future concerns including safety, efficiency, customization, scaling, and generalization. A practical decision is to treat agent deployment as an audit and safety issue, not just a tooling choice, and to track these research directions before expanding autonomy.
explain_practitioner: This survey organizes existing work on chain of thought reasoning in large language models. It examines why and when asking a model to produce reasoning steps before an answer helps, and it reviews changes in how that method is designed. It then connects these reasoning techniques to the development of self directed language agents that can follow instructions and perform actions in environments. The key result is a structured account of the path from reasoning prompts to agent behavior, plus an agenda for future work on generalization, efficiency, customization, scaling, and safety. A linked repository collects related papers.
